title: Security evidence playlist and acceptance orchestra for enterprise onboarding
creator: Asha Patel
description: Consolidated product requirement and signoff checklist that turns security controls (SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logging, KMS/HSM) into verifiable evidence artifacts for enterprise customer onboarding and private/VPC deployments. The document defines acceptance gates, required artifacts, test instructions, and the approval flow for operator and legal signoff.
background: Enterprise customers frequently request a defensible set of artifacts demonstrating Redwood meets their security and compliance requirements for private deployments. Current onboarding is ad hoc: engineering provides answers in threads and security curates separate spreadsheets. This ticket creates a reproducible, minimal evidence set and an operational playbook so onboarding time and risk are reduced.
goals: Define a concise, repeatable evidence ledger for SSO/SAML integration (IdP metadata, SAML metadata exchange proof, test assertions)
Specify RBAC mapping and operator role checklist for private control planes and on-prem installers
Enumerate audit log coverage requirements and sample log payloads for token/event types required by customers
List KMS/HSM integration modes, key lifecycle evidence, and operator test cases for CMK/HSM-backed encryption
Provide a signoff matrix indicating which RW teams must approve each evidence item (Security, Product, Infra, Legal, Customer Success)
scope: All private/VPC and on-prem deployment customer onboarding checklists
Requirements that interact with customer-managed IdPs (SAML/SOAP exchanges, SSO metadata validation)
KMS integrations supported today: AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, and HSM operator-run (SoftHSM/PKCS#11)
out_of_scope: Hosted API (public multitenant) onboarding artifacts — those remain the hosted product guide
Deep legal contract negotiation; we provide standard evidence but not final conformance statements to replace customer legal review
Unsupported legacy keying modes or expired integrations (e.g., deprecated cipher suites)
acceptance_criteria: For SSO/SAML: a reproducible test that authenticates a test user via customer IdP and captures SAML assertion logs + IdP metadata. Evidence: signed assertion sample, IdP certificate fingerprint, test run checklist
For RBAC: documented role map for operator roles and tenant roles, plus an automated smoke test that performs 5 role-bound actions and produces audit entries
For Audit Logs: sample event stream (JSON lines) for auth events, token issuance, model route changes, and KMS operations, and retention/forwarding configuration proof
For KMS/HSM: end-to-end key wrap/unseal test that uses customer CMK or HSM-provided key, with signed evidence of key ID, encryption/decryption payloads, and rotation snapshot
All artifacts labeled, placed in the onboarding evidence repository, and reviewed by Security and Infra. Approval from Customer Success confirming artifacts sufficient for a named pilot customer
deliverables: Playbook: step-by-step runbook for generating each artifact and running the verification tests
A set of example artifacts (SAML assertion, sample audit logs, KMS test outputs) redacted for PII
Automation scripts for the RBAC smoke tests (CI job) and KMS wrap/unwrap tests
Signoff matrix and checklist that can be attached to a customer onboarding packet
test_plan: Create a disposable test tenant and IdP sandbox (Okta/ADFS) and execute SAML exchange; capture assertion and verify signature chain
Run RBAC smoke tests in a staging private control plane and validate that all actions generate expected audit log entries
Execute KMS wrap/unwrap with both cloud KMS (AWS/GCP) and a lab HSM (SoftHSM) and verify key IDs and ciphertexts are logged
Replay sample audit logs to the customer SIEM endpoint (or S3/Cloud Logging) and confirm field mappings
Perform a dry-run onboarding with Customer Success using the evidence ledger and collect feedback
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Publish the evidence ledger and playbook internally and run 2 pilot onboardings (internal demo and one customer). Phase 2: Iterate artifacts based on pilot feedback, add automation jobs into onboarding CI, and train Solutions Engineering. Phase 3: Make the ledger the canonical onboarding artifact for new private deployments and link it from the Console onboarding flow.
dependencies: ENG-70134: RBAC audit hook delivery and event schema stabilization
ENG-71588: KMS/HSM operator integration and key rotation APIs
SEC-4021: Security review and threat model signoff
SEC-4082: PII redaction guidance for sample artifacts
CS-5020: Customer Success readiness and pilot commitment
risks: Customer-specific IdP quirks may require custom artifacts beyond the ledger; increases onboarding time
KMS/HSM test automation may not cover all vendor-specific behaviors (HSM PKCS#11 variations)
Audit log volume and retention differences across customers could complicate a standard artifact set
Legal may request additional attestations that require SLA changes or product work
